clientSeedGenerator.A: "audit" + 6 bytes of crypto.getRandomValues as hex (browser CSPRNG)

captures.tileOrderGenerator: crypto.getRandomValues Fisher-Yates over tiles 1..25 per round (rejection-sampled), the first `depth` opened in that order

clientSeedGenerator.A: "audit" + 6 bytes of crypto.getRandomValues as hex (browser CSPRNG)
clientSeedGenerator.D: "pfaudit-prod-mines-d<k>-" + 6 bytes of crypto.getRandomValues as hex, k = 1..5, one per Phase D epoch, drawn when the plan is built (written into the meta before the anchor rotation), submitted at the rotation that opens that epoch

captures.tileOrderGenerator: crypto.getRandomValues Fisher-Yates over tiles 1..25 per round (rejection-sampled), the first `depth` opened in that order

clientSeedGenerator.A: "audit" + 6 bytes of crypto.getRandomValues as hex (browser CSPRNG)

captures.tileOrderGenerator: crypto.getRandomValues Fisher-Yates over tiles 1..25 per round (rejection-sampled), the first `depth` opened in that order

conversion.merge: the captures are concatenated in the order of convert/inputs.mines.json; epoch = the capture's own epoch number + the number of epochs in the captures before it; capture (1-based) and captureEpoch keep the original; no bet is dropped, reordered or edited
conversion.perCapture: each capture is converted by convert() exactly as the single-capture converter does (same seed-record and bet mapping, see the fields below), then tagged

tags.phaseId: the runner's phase id (rec.phaseId; the 9 Nov file predates the field and is phase A throughout)
tags.fiatCurrency: the served settleRaw.fiatCurrency (equal to the place-bet reply's, checked)
tags.autoFinish: true where the settled reply is the open-tile reply carrying autoFinish true (no cash-out request exists for the round)

conversion.amounts: betAmount / winningAmount are the served fiat figures in fiatCurrency, not converted; the wallet currency amounts (betAmountWallet, winningAmountWallet, exchangeRate) are in the captures only
conversion.chain: each capture has its own pre-capture anchor (captures[].preCapture) and its own commitment chain; the captures are separate runs and no link between one capture's last epoch and the next capture's anchor is recorded or claimed
conversion.seedRecords: one per epoch: clientSeed, hashedServerSeed, nextHashedServerSeed, nonceStart from the rotation reply that opened the epoch (epoch 0: the one that closed the pre-capture pair), serverSeed from the rotation reply that closed it; at = that opening rotation; nonceEnd = the last nonce this capture recorded in the epoch; commitVerified = sha256(serverSeed) === hashedServerSeed and chainLinkOk = nextHashedServerSeed === the hash the closing rotation made active, both recomputed by the converter

bets.served: from settleRaw (the settling reply): id, mineCount, openTiles, mineTiles, nonce, clientSeed, serverSeedId, betAmount, winningAmount, multiplier (wins only; the loss reply has none, as on QA), result; each equal to the runner's rec field (checked, the converter throws otherwise)
bets.plan: reveals = the planned depth (spec.depth) of the round, as the QA field: tiles PLANNED, not opened
bets.captureWritten: hashedServerSeed = the epoch commitment from the rotation reply that opened the epoch (the mines replies carry no seed hash; the QA capture wrote it the same way)
bets.recorded: at, epoch, phase = the runner's record of the round

recomputed.localMines: src/rng.ts revealMines(revealed seed, clientSeed, nonce, mineCount)

servedWhenPresent.currentGameSettings: the served JSON string, copied where the settling reply carries it (as the QA dataset did on some rows)
